name: We Be Summing
description: You are given an array $$$a$$$ of length $$$n$$$ and an integer $$$k$$$. Call a non-empty array $$$b$$$ of length $$$m$$$ epic if there exists an integer $$$i$$$ where $$$1 \le i \lt m$$$ and $$$\min(b_1,\ldots,b_i) + \max(b_{i + 1},\ldots,b_m) = k$$$. Count the number of epic subarrays$$$^{\text{∗}}$$$ of $$$a$$$. $$$^{\text{∗}}$$$An array $$$a$$$ is a subarray of an array $$$b$$$ if $$$a$$$ can be obtained from $$$b$$$ by the deletion of several (possibly, zero or all) elements from the beginning and several (possibly, zero or all) elements from the end.
input_specification: The first line contains an integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$) — the number of testcases. The first line of each testcase contains integers $$$n$$$ and $$$k$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$; $$$n \lt k \lt 2 \cdot n$$$) — the length of the array $$$a$$$ and $$$k$$$. The second line of each testcase contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le n$$$). The sum of $$$n$$$ across all testcases does not exceed $$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each testcase, output the number of epic contiguous subarrays of $$$a$$$.
approach_summary: Exploit monotonicity of two-pointer invariant [L, R]. Advance R while shifting L forward to maintain validity, running in O(N) amortized time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 2064F — We Be Summing [34. Two Pointers]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: When scanning contiguous subarrays or paired indices, advancing the right pointer $R$ monotonically tightens or relaxes the constraint, allowing the left pointer $L$ to only advance forward without ever needing to reset backwards.
